correctness.rationale: Absorption before the next reversal has probability at least exp(−ℓ) after each reversal, yielding a geometric tail for N and analytic count cumulants at z=1. In distance units λ/v the first-step generator gives f'_+=f_+−zf_- and f'_-=zf_+−f_-, with one absorbing value at each outgoing velocity. The transfer matrix squares to (1−z²)I; its (1,1) coefficient A_q=cosh(qw)+sinh(qw)/w gives the right numerator. Applying the transfer first from the left endpoint and then across the remaining h gives the other numerator z sinh(hw)/w, with common denominator A_ℓ. Both event probabilities are positive for 0<s<1 and parity agrees with the outgoing direction. In the difference of conditional count cumulant generators, the normalized common denominator cancels. Expanding the log of the residual left/right ratio at z=e^θ, y=1−e^(2θ), verifies both rational formulas, including the deterministic +1 contribution to Δ_m but not to Δ_V. Their increasing q-parts have strictly positive derivatives (the numerators are 2q(q²+3q+3) and 4q³(q³+6q²+15q+15)); their decreasing h-parts enter with minus signs. The left limits are 1−ℓ²/3 and −2(ℓ⁴+15ℓ²)/45, and the right limits are strictly positive. This gives exactly the asserted threshold domains, including no interior mean zero at ℓ=√3. With u=q+1 the differences become (u²−h²+2/u)/3 and 2[(u²−h²)(u²+h²+15)−20u−6/u+10/u²]/45. Substitution of the mean zero gives −(4/15)(4u+6/u−1/u²)<0. The small-ℓ variance gap divided by 2ℓ²/3 converges uniformly to 3s²−(1−s)². For large ℓ let M=ℓ+1 and d=u−h, so s=1/2−1/(2ℓ)+d/(2ℓ). Evaluate at d=c/M²: the scaled mean equation tends to c+4, and the scaled variance equation to c/2−10, with errors O(M^−2) uniformly for bounded c. Bracketing and the nonzero limiting slopes yield the coefficients −2, 10 and hence 12 in the three stated ℓ^−3 expansions with at least the claimed error. Section 1 of python /workspace/review_reproduction.py replays the cumulant identities and verifies the numerical example (0.2886751345948129, 0.4155475052942946) at ℓ=3. Finite checks are not the proof, and none of these arguments classifies elapsed-time variance or sticky/reactive endpoints.

evidence: The count tilt is E_λ[z^N e^(−p T)1_E]=U_E(p+λ(1−z);zλ) for 0<z≤1 by the Poisson stopped path-density factor. A full rate-dependent side-resolved time transform would therefore imply the marked PGFs.

The unrestricted PGFs G_L and G_0 from the interior for first hitting L and 0 obey G_L=F_R+aF_B and G_0=F_B+bF_R, where a and b are the unrestricted continuation PGFs from the opposite outward boundary states. This is the strong Markov property with multiplicative marking. Each continuation needs a reversal, so ab<1 for z<1. Thus Ratanov's one-sided count laws determine both interval transforms by solving a two-by-two system; at z=1 take limits.

The transfer or renewal identities do not contain the all-s sign classification. It requires control of the two cumulant differences, including sign of the variance gap at the mean root and separate asymptotic balances.

originality.rationale: The balance of evidence supports the paired interior mean/variance threshold theorem, not novelty of standard telegraph transforms, the classical splitting law, or the one-sided or boundary-start marked counts. The strongest inspected same-day record has exactly the right-exit boundary law and the same transfer method. Primary one-sided marked passage laws can in fact be combined to give interior two-sided PGFs. Neither of those facts establishes the global two-root comparisons and their different rates of appearance by parameter substitution.
residual_risks: Foong–Kanno full text was not accessible in the bounded scholarly review; the inspected abstract alone does not rule out further overlap. The available Ratanov text gives a concrete transform antecedent even without that full text.

value.rationale: Exit side is a natural conditioning event for a finite-speed searcher, and the reorientation burden is distinct from elapsed time. The result establishes that the two conditional rankings disagree on a computable spatial region, even though they compare the same two count laws, and explains how the region changes with persistence. At high reversal rates the disagreement is confined to a cubic-width layer; at weak rates the variance ordering alone still switches. The value is the full exact comparison and scale, not another calculation of splitting probabilities.
